question: Authorization behaviour of every Resources endpoint today (for AC-10..AC-12)
claim: All 10 Resources endpoints are minimal-API routes in ResourcesModule.Expose with bare RequireAuthorization() (no policy or role). The caller id comes from HttpContext.User.Identity.Name via GetUserId (Guid.Empty if blank). Access is checked inside handlers against the module's local read models (GroupReadModels / GroupMemberReadModels); no IModuleClient to Group Management is used. Writes (create/update/delete type and instance) are OWNER-only (group.OwnerId == caller) and throw ResourcesForbiddenException -> 403. Reads (get/list type, get/list instance) allow owner OR member, otherwise ResourcesForbiddenException('Access to this group is forbidden.') -> 403. Missing entity: GET single returns null -> Results.NotFound() (404, empty body); PUT/DELETE and create throw ResourcesDomainException('... not found.') -> 400. Instance LIST: the access check is made on groupId if supplied, else on the group of the resourceTypeId. The type filter is then ANDed with the groupId filter, so a foreign type with the caller's own groupId returns an empty list (200), not 403/404. Mapping: NotFoundException->404, ForbiddenException->403, other CustomException->400 (including ResourcesDomainException), body {errors:[{code,message}]}; ResourceTypeNameAlreadyExistsException->409 {code,message}. Existing tests assert 403 for non-owner/non-member on most endpoints, but no test covers a cross-group resourceTypeId filter on the list.

question: Exact HTTP response bodies of the Resources module today (baseline for AC-10..AC-12)
claim: (1) ErrorHandlerMiddleware catches the exception and calls IExceptionCompositionRoot.Map. ExceptionCompositionRoot first runs all NON-default mappers (every IExceptionToResponseMapper that is not ExceptionToResponseMapper, e.g. Resources and ManagementGroups mappers) and takes SingleOrDefault of non-null results. If none returns non-null (module mapper returns null), it falls back to the shared ExceptionToResponseMapper. If the response is null, the middleware sets 500 and writes no body. (2a) ResourcesForbiddenException derives from ForbiddenException, so the shared mapper gives 403 with body {"errors":[{"code":"resources_forbidden","message":"Access to this group is forbidden."}]}. (2b) ResourcesDomainException derives from CustomException, so 400 with {"errors":[{"code":"resources_domain","message":"Resource type not found."}]}. The code is type.Name.Underscore() (Humanizer) with "_exception" removed. (2c) ResourceTypeNameAlreadyExistsException is handled by the Resources mapper: 409 with a bare top-level object {"code":"RESOURCE_TYPE_NAME_TAKEN","message":"A schema with this name already exists in the group."}, not wrapped in errors. Property casing: the shared mapper uses records Error(Code, Message) and ErrorsResponse(Errors) written via WriteAsJsonAsync(response) with no explicit options. No ConfigureHttpJsonOptions, AddJsonOptions or naming policy was found in Shared/Bootstrapper for this path, so the casing is the ASP.NET default for WriteAsJsonAsync (camelCase: errors/code/message). This default is framework behaviour that I did not verify in code. The Resources mapper's anonymous object uses lowercase names code and message literally. (3) Integration tests asserting on a Resources error BODY: UpdateResourceType_DuplicateAmongOthers_Returns409 (UpdateResourceTypeEndpointTests.cs:60, Assert.Equal("RESOURCE_TYPE_NAME_TAKEN", errorBody.Code) plus non-empty Message at :61) and CreateResourceType_DuplicateNameInGroup_Returns409 (CreateResourceTypeEndpointTests.cs:64, same literal; :65 non-empty Message). They deserialize a top-level ErrorBody(Code, Message) with PropertyNameCaseInsensitive. No test in backend/src asserts resources_forbidden, resources_domain, or any message text containing "resource type"; the other tests (e.g. UpdateDeleteResourceTypeTests.cs:162 UpdateResourceType_WithUnknownId_Returns400) assert status only. Other ReadAsStringAsync uses in the Resources tests only read 201 success bodies. Outside Resources, GROUP_NAME_TAKEN is asserted by ManagementGroups tests, which are not Resources. (4) Resources endpoints use .RequireAuthorization() with no named policy (ResourcesModule.cs:50 onward, 101, 111). The only AddAuthorization call (Shared.Infrastructure/Auth/Extensions.cs:190-196) registers per-module named policies and sets no FallbackPolicy or DefaultPolicy. Pipeline order is UseAuthentication, UseContext, UseLogging, UseRouting, UseAuthorization (Shared.Infrastructure/Extensions.cs:167-171). Test GetResourceInstances_WithoutJwt_Returns401 (GetResourceInstanceTests.cs:214-223) asserts Unauthorized on GET /resources/instances?groupId=<guid>, and asserts status only. The 401 response body cannot be determined statically; no body assertion exists. (5) GetResourceInstances_AsNonMember_Returns403 (GetResourceInstanceTests.cs:256-273) creates owner, nonMember and group, then the owner creates a type 'Phone'. The act is `nonMemberClient.GetResourcesInstancesAsync(resourceTypeId: typeId)`, i.e. ONLY resourceTypeId is sent (no groupId, no includeDeleted). The test asserts HttpStatusCode.Forbidden. The test client appends includeDeleted=true only when the bool is true (ResourcesTestClient.cs:312). No test was found that sends both groupId and resourceTypeId. Of the two tests found that send includeDeleted=true, both are owner-only: GetResourceInstances_IncludeDeletedForSoftDeletedType_ReturnsPropertyValuesWithDefinitionNames (SoftDeleteResourceTypeReadPathTests.cs:75, groupId + includeDeleted, owner client) and GetResourceInstances_SoftDeletedExcludedByDefault_AndVisibleWithIncludeDeleted (GetResourceInstanceTests.cs:163, resourceTypeId + includeDeleted, owner client). So no test sends includeDeleted=true as a non-owner member. In the data provider, includeDeleted=true switches the base query from `_dbContext.ResourceInstances.Include(x => x.PropertyValues)` to `_dbContext.ResourceInstances.IgnoreQueryFilters().Include(x => x.PropertyValues)` (GetResourceInstancesQueryDataProvider.cs:30-32), which drops all global query filters. The handler authorizes owner-or-member before the query and does not branch on IncludeDeleted (GetResourceInstancesQueryHandler.cs:45-54), so a non-owner member may pass includeDeleted=true. Whether the global filter also hides instances of soft-deleted types was not checked.
